# go.test reports per package, per test, or verbosely, fails on a failing
# test, reruns only the packages a change affects (including importers and
# testdata files), and reruns failed packages until they pass.
[!exec:go] skip

bit
stdout 'suites ✔ PASS \./a \(.*2 passed\)'
stdout 'suites ✔ PASS \./b \(.*1 passed\)'
stdout 'suites ✔ PASS \./c \(.*1 passed\)'
! stdout 'suites ✔ PASS \./a/'
stdout 'tests ✔ PASS \./a/TestA '
stdout 'tests ✔ PASS \./a/TestLog '
stdout 'tests ✔ PASS \./b/TestData '
! stdout 'tests │ .*hello from the log'
stdout 'verbose ✔ PASS \./a/TestLog '
stdout 'verbose │ .*hello from the log'

bit
! stdout '▶'

# A change to a reruns it and c, which imports it, but not b.
cp a.go.broken a/a.go
! bit suites
stdout 'suites ▶ go test -json \./a \./c \(''a/a\.go'' changed\)'
stdout '2 of 3 packages affected'
stdout 'suites ✘ FAIL \./a \(.*1 passed, 1 failed\)'
stdout 'suites ✘ FAIL \./c '
stdout 'a_test\.go:\d+: A\(\) = 5'
stderr 'test target ''suites'' failed'

# Failed packages run again until they pass.
! bit suites
stdout 'suites ▶ go test -json \./a \./c \(previously failed\)'
cp a.go.fixed a/a.go
bit suites
stdout 'suites ✔ PASS \./a '
stdout 'suites ✔ PASS \./c '

# A testdata file is an input of the package that holds it.
cp want.txt.changed b/testdata/want.txt
! bit suites
stdout 'suites ▶ go test -json \./b \(''b/testdata/want\.txt'' changed\)'
stdout '1 of 3 packages affected'
stdout 'b_test\.go:\d+: testdata = "changed\\n"'

-- BUILD.bit --
suites = go.test {
  package = "./..."
}

tests = go.test {
  package = "./..."
  report  = "tests"
}

verbose = go.test {
  package = "./a"
  report  = "verbose"
}
-- go.mod --
module example.com/m

go 1.22
-- a/a.go --
package a

func A() int { return 1 }
-- a.go.broken --
package a

func A() int { return 5 }
-- a.go.fixed --
package a

func A() int { return 1 }

func Unused() {}
-- a/a_test.go --
package a

import "testing"

func TestA(t *testing.T) {
	if got := A(); got != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("A() = %d", got)
	}
}

func TestLog(t *testing.T) { t.Log("hello from the log") }
-- b/b.go --
package b
-- b/b_test.go --
package b

import (
	"os"
	"testing"
)

func TestData(t *testing.T) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile("testdata/want.txt")
	if err != nil || string(data) != "ok\n" {
		t.Fatalf("testdata = %q, %v", data, err)
	}
}
-- b/testdata/want.txt --
ok
-- want.txt.changed --
changed
-- c/c.go --
package c

import "example.com/m/a"

func C() int { return a.A() + 1 }
-- c/c_test.go --
package c

import "testing"

func TestC(t *testing.T) {
	if C() != 2 {
		t.Fatal("C() != 2")
	}
}
